links.note: English names Jesus, the subject implicit in “said.”
The dative expresses staying with someone.
English renders the explanatory “and” as “for.”
Greek “from a distance” is rendered “a long way.”
The genitive expresses the bread used to satisfy them.
The noun means leftovers or surplus.
English names the group implicit in “they were.”
Greek “if” introduces a forceful negative oath.
The participle means embarking, which implies entering a boat.
Greek “except” is recast as “more than.”
English changes indirect “they have” to direct “we have.”
Greek asks whether they “have” a hardened heart.
Greek leaves the feeding verb implicit from the preceding question.
The genitive marks the hand being grasped.
English changes direct “you see” to indirect “he saw.”
English renders the general “all things” as “everyone.”
English recasts the coordinated subjects as “with.”
The impersonal verb means “it is necessary.”
The dative noun expresses speaking with openness.
Greek uses an article for “the things.”
The same Greek preposition governs both reasons.
